summary: Backend-only testing of Stripe checkout, freemium quota gating, SEO sitemap, and admin flag for Casino Spotter. Created /app/backend/tests/test_stripe_freemium_seo.py with 14 pytest cases. 12 PASS, 2 FAIL (both blocked by EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget exhaustion at $0.40/$0.40 cap — not application bugs). Verified: /auth/me returns new freemium fields, legitimacy 1st call=200 / 2nd call=402, quota is per-user, premium flag bypasses 402, Stripe checkout creates valid checkout.stripe.com session and persists payment_transactions, /api/sitemap.xml returns valid XML with content-type application/xml containing 6 static URLs + 8 technique URLs + dynamic report URLs, admin user is_admin=true via ADMIN_EMAIL match.

critical.issue: Returns 500 immediately after a fresh successful checkout creation. Emergent's stripe proxy responds with 404 'No such checkout.session: cs_test_...' when retrieving a session it just created via the same sk_test_emergent key. Same /api/integrations.emergentagent.com endpoint is hit for both create and retrieve but retrieve fails. This blocks payment confirmation flow (success URL handler will receive 500 instead of {status, payment_status, ...}). Reproduction in iteration_4.json under rca. Library: emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.get_checkout_status -> stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve(...).

Returns 500 due to EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget exhaustion ('Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 0.4073, Max budget: 0.4'). Quota gate logic itself is correct (verified via legitimacy endpoint), but cannot validate analysis quota end-to-end until budget reset. NOTE: consume_free_quota runs BEFORE the LLM call (line 397) so the counter increments even though the LLM later fails; a free user whose 1st upload errored on LLM will be charged a quota use and locked out — consider reverting the counter on LLM failure or moving the increment to a post-success step.

minor.issue: Base URL is hardcoded to 'https://scam-spotter-casino.preview.emergentagent.com' (line 982). Will break on prod deploy under a different domain. Use env var or request host.
Lives at /api/sitemap.xml — search engines and tools (and robots.txt) typically expect /sitemap.xml at the site root. Consider proxying or also exposing at the apex path.

PREMIUM_MONTHLY_USD is hardcoded ($9.99). origin_url accepts any value from the client (success_url/cancel_url construction). Recommend validating origin_url against an allowlist to prevent open-redirect via Stripe success page.
No upper rate limit per user — a user could mass-create sessions and pollute payment_transactions.
Increments counter even if downstream LLM/file processing fails, leading to quota burn on transient errors. Either decrement on failure or move to a post-success step.

rca of the issue: Stripe status 500 RCA: POST /api/stripe/checkout calls emergentintegrations.StripeCheckout.create_checkout_session(sk_test_emergent) which proxies via https://integrations.emergentagent.com/stripe/v1/checkout/sessions and returns a real cs_test_... id and a hosted checkout.stripe.com URL. The follow-up GET /api/stripe/checkout/status/{session_id} re-instantiates StripeCheckout (different webhook_url since both use same base_url) and calls stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve, which is patched to hit https://integrations.emergentagent.com/stripe/v1/checkout/sessions/{id} but the proxy returns 404 resource_missing for the very session it returned. Likely the proxy only allows retrieval within a specific scope/account-key the create call used (perhaps the create call was scoped to a per-request emergent virtual account and the retrieve call lands on a different scope). Mitigation: (a) cache session metadata locally on create (already partially done in payment_transactions — main agent can return that as a fallback if proxy 404s), (b) report to emergent support, (c) try keeping the StripeCheckout instance per-session via a module-level cache. Confirmed reproducible by curl POST /stripe/checkout then GET /stripe/checkout/status/{id} — see backend.err.log lines around 14:24:38.
